regions.text: のうちにも「あの日あなたの處へ行つたのは側然どは思でない無がします」（※三様）といふ言葉がある。

quote.translation: In Mushanokōji Saneatsu's His Sister there is likewise the line, "I have a feeling that my going to your place that day was not by chance" (Act III).

regions.text: 「偶然にして偶然でないをか偶然とは思へないをかいふのは、「目約なき1目的の下肢の強護の除り上肢が殆ど響を失つた形である。

quote.translation: Expressions such as "by chance and yet not by chance" or "it cannot be thought chance" are forms in which the second member of "purposeless / purpose" is emphasised so strongly that the first has almost lost its resonance.

regions.text: 心理學者アンリビェロンは「偶然論一概念の心理學」（HenriPieron,Essaisurlehasrd：lapychoiogied'unconcepe）といふ論文の中で、偶然性のこの方面を特に力説してるる。

quote.translation: The psychologist Henri Piéron, in his essay "Essay on chance: the psychology of a concept" (Henri Piéron, Essai sur le hasard: la psychologie d'un concept), lays particular stress on this aspect of contingency.

regions.text: 彼に従へば、湖酔を通つてゐてそこにポートがあつても別に偶然とは云はない。

quote.translation: According to Piéron, if we are walking by a lake and there is a boat there, we do not especially call this chance.

regions.text: ボートを酒いで遊びたいといふ強い欲望をその瞬間に有つてゐたとして初めてそれを幸福な偶然と云ふのである。

quote.translation: Only if at that instant we had a strong wish to go out rowing do we call it a "happy chance".

regions.text: 道を歩いてるて猫が前を横切つてもそれを別段偶然とはしない。

quote.translation: Again, if a cat crosses our path as we walk along the road, we do not especially treat this as chance.

regions.text: 白轉車乗りが自動車を避けようとした途端に猫にふつかつて猫を轢き変したとすればその時に初めてその猫を道へ置いた「不幸な偶然を恬むのである。

quote.translation: But if a cyclist, just as he swerves to avoid a car, runs into a cat and kills it, then, and only then, does he curse the "unhappy chance" that put the cat in the road.

regions.text: ピエロジは斯くして偶然には「主視踊心」（interetsub-jectif）が重要な契機をなしてるるとして、偶然の現象の「主觀側画」（cotesubjcctif）または「人間的要素」（clcmenthumain）を强彌してゐるが、心理學者の説として興味

quote.translation: Piéron accordingly holds that "subjective interest" (intérêt subjectif) forms an important moment in chance, and he emphasises the "subjective side" (côté subjectif) or "human element" (élément humain) of the phenomenon of chance, a view of interest as the theory of a psychologist (Revue de Métaphysique et de Morale, 1902, p. 688-691).
